about.title: About Body Fat Calculator
about.description: The Body Fat Calculator estimates body fat percentage using measurement methods including waist circumference, hip measurements, and other body dimensions. Body fat percentage can provide a broader body-composition reference than BMI alone. Understanding body composition can help with fitness goal setting and progress tracking alongside other health measures.

howTo.title: How to Use the Body Fat Calculator

steps.title: Select Method and Gender
steps.description: Choose your gender and preferred measurement method (Navy, Army, or YMCA).

steps.title: Take Body Measurements
steps.description: Measure required body dimensions like waist, neck, and hips using a flexible measuring tape.

steps.title: Enter Personal Data
steps.description: Input your age, weight, and the measurements you took.

steps.title: Review Results
steps.description: View your estimated body fat percentage, reference category, and general interpretation guidance.

tips: Measure at the same time of day for consistency
Use a flexible measuring tape and measure consistently each time
Take measurements on bare skin when possible

faq.q: What's a healthy body fat percentage for men and women?
faq.a: Reference ranges vary by source, age, sex, and context. General adult categories are often presented differently across methods, so use the calculator as a reference tool rather than a medical assessment.

faq.q: How should I interpret body fat calculator estimates?
faq.a: Body fat calculators provide estimates, and results can vary based on the method used and how measurements are taken. If you need a more rigorous assessment, consider discussing measurement options with a qualified provider or specialist.

faq.q: How do body fat measurement methods differ?
faq.a: Different methods can produce different estimates. The calculator offers multiple methods so you can compare outputs and use them as general body-composition references.

faq.q: How often should I measure my body fat percentage?
faq.a: People often track body fat periodically rather than daily because hydration, food intake, and measurement technique can affect the result. Consistent timing and method can make comparisons more useful.

faq.q: Is body fat percentage more important than BMI?
faq.a: Body fat percentage and BMI describe different things, so some people look at both as general reference measures. Neither metric should be treated as a complete assessment of health or body composition on its own.

faq.q: How do I take body measurements for the calculator?
faq.a: Use a flexible measuring tape and follow the measurement instructions for the method you selected. Taking measurements the same way each time can make comparisons more consistent.
